candidates.label: Softer lip transition and less exposed teeth
candidates.review: The lip border is less drawn-on and the shorter tooth row is gentler, but the eyes and nasal mound remain generic. No meaningful overall likeness gain yet.

stats.designLabel: Softer lip transition and less exposed teeth

candidates.label: Flatter cheek plane and narrower nasal mound
candidates.review: The cheek plane is less spherical and the narrower nasal mound improves the three-quarter view. The broad forehead and open white eye shapes still dominate.

stats.designLabel: Flatter cheek plane and narrower nasal mound

candidates.label: Closer-set eyes and fuller lower eyelid
candidates.review: Closer eye spacing and reduced scleral brightness give a calmer expression. The larger lower-lid patch is coherent, but the original nasal silhouette is still too blunt.

stats.designLabel: Closer-set eyes and fuller lower eyelid

candidates.label: Integrated anatomy, lips and eye proportions
candidates.review: The combined eye, cheek and lip adjustments are the most balanced of this set in both views. Select as the next design baseline; head length and neck exposure still need correction.

stats.designLabel: Integrated anatomy, lips and eye proportions

candidates.label: Shorter, fuller head proportions
candidates.review: The shorter head helps the body ratio, but the combined width and chin expansion make the face too broad and flat. Do not select this combination.

stats.designLabel: Shorter, fuller head proportions

candidates.label: Reduced neck exposure and raised collar fit
candidates.review: Reduced neck exposure and the higher collar improve the full figure. The stronger head roll is plausible, although the original long facial proportions remain.

stats.designLabel: Reduced neck exposure and raised collar fit

candidates.label: Softer chin and slimmer nasal bridge
candidates.review: The nasal bridge is less blunt and the chin reads softer. The face is more balanced, but the neck still looks stretched above the collar.

stats.designLabel: Softer chin and slimmer nasal bridge

candidates.label: Integrated skull, neck and nose correction
candidates.review: The moderate skull shortening, neck reduction and nasal change work best together. The face remains generic, but the full-body proportion is less doll-like. Select this integrated version.

stats.designLabel: Integrated skull, neck and nose correction

candidates.label: Gentler, narrower smile
candidates.review: The narrower smile is gentler, but it loses some of the reference's cheerful openness. Profile review reveals the chin remains too recessed relative to the mouth and nose.

stats.designLabel: Gentler, narrower smile

candidates.label: Recessed oral cavity and rounded lips
candidates.review: The oral recess has genuine depth, but the larger lip projection and dark opening make the mouth heavier. The profile still needs a stronger chin rather than more lip volume.

stats.designLabel: Recessed oral cavity and rounded lips

candidates.label: Lifted smile corners and softened nasal crease
candidates.review: Raised corners make the expression brighter, although the thinner lip transition looks slightly stretched at the ends. The profile limitation remains.

stats.designLabel: Lifted smile corners and softened nasal crease

candidates.label: Moderate cavity depth and balanced smile
candidates.review: The moderate cavity and narrower smile are the most natural combination here. Retain the restrained lip volume; next correct the recessed chin and nasal/profile balance.

stats.designLabel: Moderate cavity depth and balanced smile

candidates.label: Moderate chin projection
candidates.review: Moderate chin projection improves the side silhouette, but the lower face still tapers backward more than desired. It is a conservative improvement, not a complete correction.

stats.designLabel: Moderate chin projection

candidates.label: Stronger chin and reduced nasal tip
candidates.review: The strongest chin setting creates a conspicuous lower-face bulge in three-quarter view. Reject the larger projection despite the less recessed profile.

stats.designLabel: Stronger chin and reduced nasal tip

candidates.label: Forward chin with softer brow ridge
candidates.review: The softer brow ridge and nasal bridge are helpful, but the broad cheek flattening and chin together make the mouth-to-jaw transition too uniform.

stats.designLabel: Forward chin with softer brow ridge

candidates.label: Balanced lower-face and nasal contour
candidates.review: This is the best compromise: the chin supports the mouth without a large bulb, and the nose/profile balance is improved. The ear still looks like stacked simple primitives and is the next visible defect.

stats.designLabel: Balanced lower-face and nasal contour

candidates.label: Curved auricle, helix and conchal bowl
candidates.review: Reject. The conchal shell intersects the scalp hair, leaving only a bright helix ring visible from the side. The larger ear makes this defect especially obvious.

stats.designLabel: Curved auricle, helix and conchal bowl

candidates.label: Smaller auricle with backward upper tilt
candidates.review: Reject. Reducing the ear size does not solve the dark hair intersection inside the ear. The outline looks like a separate loop rather than a filled auricle.

stats.designLabel: Smaller auricle with backward upper tilt

candidates.label: Moderate ear size and quieter skin tint
candidates.review: Reject. The skin tint is quieter, but the central bowl is still hidden by the hair cap. Correct the scalp boundary and ear attachment before accepting this topology.

stats.designLabel: Moderate ear size and quieter skin tint

candidates.label: Compact ear and softer helix presentation
candidates.review: Reject. Tilt changes do not resolve the underlying ear/scalp overlap. Keep C16 as the selected design and repair the anatomical shell placement.

stats.designLabel: Compact ear and softer helix presentation

candidates.label: Raised scalp boundary and exposed concha
candidates.review: The conchal bowl is now visible and the ear has actual cartilage structure instead of a ring. This is the best of the set, although the attachment still needs a small connective skin volume.

stats.designLabel: Raised scalp boundary and exposed concha

candidates.label: Shallower hair notch and outward ear fit
candidates.review: The shallower hair notch works, but the greater outward offset makes the ear look more detached in three-quarter view. Do not use the larger outset.

stats.designLabel: Shallower hair notch and outward ear fit

candidates.label: Compact ear with wider scalp clearance
candidates.review: The compact ear is acceptable, but the larger hair clearance makes the side hairline too sharply notched. It reduces the natural swept-back silhouette.

stats.designLabel: Compact ear with wider scalp clearance

candidates.label: Balanced auricle and swept-back hairline
candidates.review: The cartilage is coherent, but the combination of outward offset and extra notch is slightly less natural than C21. Retain the more conservative fit.

stats.designLabel: Balanced auricle and swept-back hairline

candidates.label: Lower swept fringe over the left brow
candidates.review: Lower fringe coverage is closer to the reference and the attached ears are less disconnected. The sweep remains rather flat across the brow.

rebuild.designLabel: Lower swept fringe over the left brow

stats.designLabel: Lower swept fringe over the left brow

candidates.label: Deeper sweep with a narrower part opening
candidates.review: The deeper sweep approaches the upper eyelid and compresses the forehead too much. Keep more clearance above the left eye.

rebuild.designLabel: Deeper sweep with a narrower part opening

stats.designLabel: Deeper sweep with a narrower part opening

candidates.label: Shallow fringe with individual edge breakup
candidates.review: The larger periodic edge variation creates visible scallops rather than natural wispy tips. Reject the stronger sinusoidal edge breakup.

rebuild.designLabel: Shallow fringe with individual edge breakup

stats.designLabel: Shallow fringe with individual edge breakup

candidates.label: Balanced brow coverage and lifted hair volume
candidates.review: Moderate coverage and slight lifted volume create the best swept silhouette in this set. Select it; the next major issue is the broad plastic-looking hair reflection rather than the outline.

rebuild.designLabel: Balanced brow coverage and lifted hair volume

stats.designLabel: Balanced brow coverage and lifted hair volume

candidates.label: Across-strand anisotropic reflection
candidates.review: The reflection is more directional, but the across-strand highlight creates a broad band along the fringe edge and emphasizes the separate ponytail ribbons.

stats.designLabel: Across-strand anisotropic reflection

candidates.label: Along-strand anisotropic reflection
candidates.review: The along-strand direction is more plausible, but the stronger highlight exposes the change in tangent direction at the fringe root. The surface still looks too glossy.

stats.designLabel: Along-strand anisotropic reflection

candidates.label: Fine directional sheen with tighter highlights
candidates.review: The tighter high-anisotropy reflection makes the ponytail tresses look like shiny cords. Reject the more aggressive sheen.

rebuild.designLabel: Fine directional sheen with tighter highlights

stats.designLabel: Fine directional sheen with tighter highlights

candidates.label: Softer directional sheen and reduced coating
candidates.review: The softer directional sheen and low clear coating reduce the plastic appearance while retaining readable strands. Select the restrained material; hair volume and tip breakup remain the next priorities.

rebuild.designLabel: Softer directional sheen and reduced coating

stats.designLabel: Softer directional sheen and reduced coating

candidates.label: Light curved strand layering
candidates.review: Reject. The added strand sheets create conspicuous pale reflective streaks in the rear view. Front detail is finer, but the back is not acceptable.

stats.designLabel: Light curved strand layering

candidates.label: Full layered strands and tapered ends
candidates.review: Reject. More coverage increases the bright sheet-like artifacts behind the ponytails. The cards need a different material response before density can be judged.

rebuild.designLabel: Full layered strands and tapered ends

stats.designLabel: Full layered strands and tapered ends

candidates.label: Denser strand coverage with quieter wave
candidates.review: Reject. The dense layer looks like strips of reflective paper from behind. The rear scalp also ends in an unnaturally straight line, now obvious in this audit view.

rebuild.designLabel: Denser strand coverage with quieter wave

stats.designLabel: Denser strand coverage with quieter wave

candidates.label: Moderate strand density and natural tip spread
candidates.review: Reject. The moderate density has a better front silhouette, but the same bright back-facing artifacts remain. Keep C32 and repair material response and nape shape.

rebuild.designLabel: Moderate strand density and natural tip spread

stats.designLabel: Moderate strand density and natural tip spread

candidates.label: Unlit strand diagnostic with curved nape
candidates.review: The unlit diagnostic removes the pale rear streaks, confirming the texture itself is dark. It also removes too much dimensional shading, so it is not the production choice.

rebuild.designLabel: Unlit strand diagnostic with curved nape

stats.designLabel: Unlit strand diagnostic with curved nape

candidates.label: Low-reflection physical strand layers
candidates.review: The physical low-reflection cards fix the bright strips and the curved nape is more natural than the earlier straight cut. Fine detail remains restrained and coherent.

stats.designLabel: Low-reflection physical strand layers

candidates.label: Moderate strand density and gathered flow
candidates.review: The stronger coverage hides too much of the volumetric tress shape, while the deeper nape approaches a heavy bob-like edge. Prefer a lighter layer.

stats.designLabel: Moderate strand density and gathered flow

candidates.label: Fine outer strands with restrained nape length
candidates.review: The lighter strand coverage and shorter curved nape best preserve volume while adding finer edge detail. Select this version; the ponytail trajectory still needs a less rigid diagonal bend.
